title: A conflict, in the road planners' words

blocks.text: A city's road-resurfacing model names its rows like this, and its conflict finder returns a list of such names. The council's planners want each one as a sentence. The table gives the exact sentence for each kind of row:

rows: `R12 Elm Street must be done this plan.`
`The north district has 3 paving crews in 2027.`
`R07 Mill Lane must finish before R12 Elm Street starts.`

blocks.text: A district with one crew gets the singular: `The west district has 1 paving crew in 2029.` A row of a known kind that names a job, year or district missing from the data (`need_R99` when `jobs` has no `R99`) gets the same fallback sentence as an unknown kind: `Rule need_R99 has no description yet.`

`jobs` maps a job id (letters and digits, no underscores) to its street; `caps` maps a year to the resurfacing budget in $k, written with a thousands separator; `crews` maps `(district, year)` to the number of paving crews. A district name may contain underscores (`south_east`); in the sentence each underscore becomes a space.
Write `translate(conflict, jobs, caps, crews)` returning the sentences, in the conflict's order. The `sentence` helper is a good place for the per-row work. About twenty lines.

cases.says: each kind of row becomes its sentence, with the job's id and street
a district name may hold underscores, and the sentence writes them as spaces
a budget below ten thousand still gets a thousands separator
a row of an unknown kind still gets a sentence, never its raw name alone
a row that names a job, year or district the data lacks gets the fallback sentence
one crew is written in the singular

origin.section: A Planner Message Names Rules and Projects, Never Rows

concepts: a sentence per kind of row, with names, money and who set the number
